values.note: $24 per site (the same in recreation.gov's 2026-2028 tables), including two vehicles or one RV; a third vehicle is $11 a night and day use $11. Firewood $10 a bundle from the host.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/spruce-grove-campground ('$24 fee per site for overnight camping. Two vehicles or one RV per site is included in the camping fee. $11 fee for a third vehicle. $11 fee for day use'; last updated January 23, 2026) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234686/rates (2026, 2027: STANDARD NONELECTRIC 24, TENT ONLY NONELECTRIC 24) + recreation.gov notice (firewood '$10.00/bundle'), read 2026-10-26

hookups.source: campsite catalog for 234686 (all sites NONELECTRIC) + recreation.gov rate table (STANDARD NONELECTRIC / TENT ONLY NONELECTRIC only), read 2026-10-26

values.note: 26 reservable sites plus the host's: 11 standard (back-in spurs 18-36 ft; about nine take a rig of 23 ft or more) and 15 tent-only. Forest Service: maximum trailer length 35 ft. Gravel road and sites; parking inside is limited.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/spruce-grove-campground ('It has 27 campsites with parking spurs 18-36 feet and a maximum trailer length of 35 feet') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234686 ('Parking aprons fit RVs up to 35 feet in length'; 'the driveway is gravel as are the sites') + campsite catalog for 234686 (11 STANDARD NONELECTRIC + 15 TENT ONLY NONELECTRIC reservable, 002-Host MANAGEMENT; Max Vehicle Length 18-36; all Back-in), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Drinking water from a hand pump; firewood sold at the host site. Bear country: store food in the vehicle or bear-resistant containers.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234686 ('Drinking water from a hand pump, trash collection and vault toilets are among the amenities') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/spruce-grove-campground ('Facilities include toilets, table, water and fire rings'; 'Vault toilet(s)'; 'A hand pump is available'; bear closure order), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Forest Service: mid-May to mid-October, weather dependent; all services may not be available early or late. Dates are recreation.gov's 2027 fee season (2026: May 15 - Oct 11).

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/spruce-grove-campground ('This campground is open mid-May to mid-October, weather dependent'; 'Seasons of Use: Mid-May to mid-October') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234686/rates (Peak Season 2026-05-15 to 10-11, 2027-05-14 to 10-10), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Every site is reservable on recreation.gov up to 5 days before arrival; sites not reserved by then go first-come and must be occupied the same night. recreation.gov's 2-night weekend minimum is marked soft, so it may be relaxed for a booking close to the date. 14 consecutive nights at most.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234686 (notice 'Reservations are available up to 5 days prior to arrival date. Sites not reserved 5 days before become available on a first come - first serve (FF) bases.'; facility_rules reservationCutOff 5 'day(s) prior to arrival', minWeekendStay 2 'soft', maxConsecutiveStay 14) + /rates (2027 Peak 05-14 to 10-10) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/spruce-grove-campground ('No more than a 14-night consecutive stay', 'First-come, first-served sites must be occupied the same night'), read 2026-10-26

note: Beside large rock outcroppings on Tarryall Creek at 8,600 ft, with little shade among spruce and aspen; about 13 mi up Tarryall Road (CR 77) from Lake George, the entrance set back from the road (South Park RD, Pike-San Isabel NF). Trails into the Lost Creek Wilderness start across the creek bridge; Tarryall Reservoir is 11 mi away. --Claude
